_comment: Grades are the point of this file, not the commands.
MCP carries no risk vocabulary, so every MCP tool defaults to grade 'exec' —
disposition ASK, which a standing grant satisfies. Without the entries below, a
user who once approved turn_on with 'always' would have silently pre-approved
every future physical call to it, for the rest of the session and every session
carrying the same grant. 'physical' is the one grade no standing grant can reach
(kernel-design SS8): it asks every single call, every time.
The read tools are graded down deliberately and for the same safety reason, not
for convenience: a server graded physical wholesale would prompt on every
get_state too, and a user prompted forty times an hour stops reading the prompt.
Cheapening the reads is what keeps the writes worth reading.
cwd is resolved relative to this file, so ".." is the repo root: a shell running
`omni --mcp` finds the ai_server package. The Alfred bridge generates
.omni/mcp.local.json from this file with an absolute interpreter and cwd (omni-jev J7).
Every tool the two servers expose needs a decision here. Reads are listed by name;
anything not listed takes the server grade: home_assistant is 'physical' (so apply,
turn_on, turn_off, toggle, set_brightness and set_temperature ask every call);
alfred_plugins has no server grade, so its *_execute_command tools are listed as
'physical' one by one, because a plugin's effect is whatever the plugin does.
tests/test_mcp_json_grades.py fails if a tool is added without a grade.
